note: What each candidate job reads (#898). `classify` hashes the HEAD tree
filtered by these globs, and a job whose hash matches an earlier
merge-request pipeline's successful run of the same job stands on that run
instead of doing the work again.
Too broad only costs a rerun; too narrow reuses a stale result, which is a
correctness bug. Widen when in doubt.

The `image` group is what the Dockerfile's build actually consumes: the
context less the files no stage copies out of it. Test files are in the
context (`COPY . .`) but reach none of the artefacts the runner stage
copies -- web/build, web/node_modules, dist/cli/orbit.js -- so a test-only
change leaves the image identical. That exclusion is what makes reuse
worth having: the common fix after a red `fast` is a test or a fidelity
baseline, and neither changes the image.
